# `bin/limits-exec`

A tool: run it from the root of an instance (or of the kit, for the kit's own tools).
Source: [`bin/limits-exec`](../../../bin/limits-exec)

## What it says about itself

```text
bin/limits-exec RUN_DIR -- command args...

Runs a command as a worker process tree under the run's enforced limits (LESSONS.md "Limits are enforced, not promised", audit F9):
  - RUN_DIR/.limits (JSON written by bin/new-run: {"cpu_hours": H, "threads": N, "mem_gb": G}) →
    a transient systemd user scope with CPUQuota=N*100% (the tree cannot use more than N cores'
    worth of CPU, whatever the worker spawns) and MemoryMax=G G; defaults 8 / 8 / 16 when absent;
  - the whole-run CPU budget (LESSONS.md "The whole-run CPU budget is enforced"; the source's run 346 used 11.13
    CPU-hours of 8, only flagged): inside the scope a watcher reads the cgroup's cpu.stat each second; at
    cpu_hours it sends TERM to the command (so each route stops in order: timeout passes it to claude, _ext.py
    stops Codex as at its other caps), waits cpu_grace_seconds (default 30), then kills every process left in
    the scope, background jobs included. Exit 152 (128 + SIGXCPU), cpu_cap_hit=true in usage.json;
  - /usr/bin/time -v around the command → RUN_DIR/time.log (user/sys/maxrss of waited-for children);
  - the scope's cgroup cpu.stat is read just before the scope ends (from inside it, so still-running
    background children are counted too) → RUN_DIR/usage.json {cpu_seconds, user_seconds,
    system_seconds, wall_seconds, max_rss_kb, cpu_hours_cap, threads_cap, mem_gb_cap, enforced}.
If systemd-run cannot make a user scope (no user manager), the limits cannot be enforced, so nothing runs: exit 2
(P-3 B3, user 2026-10-01: RULES.md §9, limits are enforced, not promised). `limits-exec --probe` exits 0 when a user
scope can be made and 1 otherwise; bin/run-external asks it before the approval is touched.
The scope is named kit-scope-<run>-<pid>; a TERM, INT or HUP to this script stops it, so stopping a detached run's
kit-run-NAME service ends the worker too (P-12 H5: the scope lies outside the service's cgroup). The working files
stay in a temporary directory of this script's; usage.json and time.log are renamed over the run's names, never
written through a link the worker left there (P-12 C2).
Exit status is the command's, or 152 when the CPU budget stopped it. Nothing here writes outside RUN_DIR but its own
temporary working directory, removed at exit; it writes no ledger line (bin/run-external puts usage.json's figures on EXIT-EXT).
```
